prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies approved bays/circuits; supervisory/execution/protection layers cannot substitute. Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) sends Bay Status Digest to Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing), validates authority/mode/interlocks/availability, verifies outcomes, logs rejected requests, degrades stale points, uses Battery Load Test Record. Breaker Control Unit executes/returns position/health; local authority/interlocks prevail, including testing. North Bay Controller/South Bay Controller have non-substitutable authority, coordinate shared equipment; North blocks unsafe closing/preserves local control during communications loss; South reports mode/availability. Glasswing presents controls/quality, produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip, receives Protocol Retry Summary from Station Gateway; gateway preserves mappings/access/timestamps, reports faults without actuation; verify post-outage currency. Maintenance Remote Terminal requires authorization, cannot bypass safeguards, uses Settings Review Receipt from Engineering Workstation; workstation supports authorized revision-controlled review/export, not routine commands. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) independently trips, produces Relay Diagnostic Note; North Protection Panel/Transformer Protection Panel provide independent protection. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) supplies quality-marked time/Clock Drift Snapshot to Sequence Event Archive (Orchard); Orchard retains ordered, qualified audit/testing/restoration evidence, protects backups/recovery. Station DC System powers/monitors protection/control, retains Battery Load Test Record. Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) reviews settings/test/restoration; revisions require studies/approval/comparison/testing; discrepancies block release. Substation Supervisor controls communication/mapping/logic/configuration changes, coordinates timing/responsibilities with Switching Desk Coordinator (Keystone), who maintains prerequisites/sequence, produces Isolation Boundary Card, confirms handback. Control Room Operator reviews restrictions, acknowledges/logs/verifies; unresolved handoffs: Clearance Handoff Memo. Substation Field Crew locally verifies uncertain indications/discrepancies, clearances/isolation/grounding/work boundaries. Cinder verifies boundaries/reports unsafe conditions. Windows consider loading/switching/personnel. Tests require approved procedures/calibrated instruments/stop capability; preserve energized-feeder protection; operator tracks disabled functions through verified restoration. Inhibit remote commands for uncertain status/missing permissives; degraded communications invalidate remote indications until verified. Manual operation requires approved procedures/local checks/operator communication.

New part:
S218: A suspected controller or relay fault is assessed before any restart, bypass, or replacement is attempted.
S219: Restoration includes confirming normal indications, protection availability, communications status, and the removal of temporary test connections.
S220: The Substation Supervisor confirms that required records are complete and that operating restrictions are formally cleared before returning equipment to normal service.
S221: Operational assurance at Alder Creek depends on clear authority, verified equipment state, and records that support later review.
S222: The Control Room Operator remains responsible for deciding whether an automation request is appropriate for current operating conditions.
S223: The Bay Automation Controller shall execute only commands permitted by its approved logic and configured interlocks.
S224: The Feeder Protection Relay shall retain its protective function independently of supervisory communications.
S225: The Protection Relay Engineer reviews protection behavior after material changes and records any unresolved concerns for operational follow-up.
S226: The Station Supervisory Control System presents control indications and command results for operator assessment.
S227: The Sequence Event Archive retains time-ordered records needed to reconstruct significant control and protection events.
S228: The Engineering Workstation shall be used for authorized configuration work under established change control.
S229: The Satellite Time Receiver supports consistent event timing, and time-quality concerns shall be investigated before records are relied upon for sequence analysis.
S230: The Station Gateway shall maintain the defined boundary between station automation and external communications.
S231: The Station DC System shall be confirmed available before switching that depends on station control power.
S232: The Breaker Control Unit shall reject commands that do not satisfy its configured permissive conditions.
S233: Substation Field Crew uses the Isolation Boundary Card to verify the approved work boundary before entering the controlled area.
S234: Substation Field Crew reports unexpected equipment conditions promptly and pauses work when the approved boundary is uncertain.
S235: Switching Desk Coordinator receives the Clearance Handoff Memo and confirms that its clearance status agrees with the active switching record.
S236: Keystone shall confirm that switching authority, equipment state, and communication limits are understood before coordinating any automation-enabled action.
S237: The Substation Supervisor verifies that unresolved risks have an assigned owner and an agreed disposition before normal service is resumed.
S238: The Control Room Operator confirms indications locally when remote status is incomplete, inconsistent, or delayed.
S239: The Protection Relay Engineer assesses unexplained trips and abnormal protection indications before protection is returned to service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
